task.title: Getting Started with DITA - Complete Guide
task.shortdesc: This is a comprehensive sample DITA task topic to demonstrate the live preview functionality including steps and substeps with proper numbering.

taskbody.prereq: Before you begin, make sure you have access to a web browser and can edit XML files.

step.cmd: Open Web eDITA in your browser and familiarize yourself with the interface.

info.p: The interface consists of two main panes: the DITA Source pane on the left and the Live Preview pane on the right.

step.cmd: Learn about DITA highlighting elements by reviewing the examples below:

ul.li: Bold text using the b element
Italic text using the i element
Underlined text using the u element
Teletype text using tt for monospace

step.cmd: To create your own DITA content with steps and substeps, follow this process:

substep.cmd: Create a new task document using the proper DOCTYPE declaration.
Add a descriptive title and shortdesc elements.
Include a prereq element if there are prerequisites.
substep.info: Prerequisites help users understand what they need before starting the task.

substep.cmd: Structure your main content using steps elements.
Use substeps when you need to break down a complex step into smaller actions.

step.cmd: Understand different DITA elements by examining these examples:

section.title: Notes and Warnings
section.note: You can edit this content directly in the left pane and see changes in real-time!
Always validate your DITA files before publishing.
Proper structure is essential for DITA documents.

dl.dd: Main numbered actions that users need to perform, displayed as 1., 2., 3., etc.
Secondary actions within a step, displayed as a) b) c) etc.
Requirements that must be met before starting the task.

step.cmd: Test your DITA content by using the preview functionality:

substep.cmd: Make changes in the left pane editor.
Observe how the preview updates automatically in the right pane.
Notice how steps are numbered (1., 2., 3.) and substeps are lettered (a) b) c).
substep.info: The numbering and lettering happen automatically - you don't need to add numbers manually!
